messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for inference streaming endpoints (/v1/stream). p95 latency 1.2s -> 3.8s, p99 2.1s -> 12.4s over the last 10m. Error rate for streaming stall events increased to 4.7%. Auto-escalating to incidents channel.

maria: I'm seeing the same in the dashboard — spikes line up at 2026-03-14T14:22Z. A bunch of streaming tails are stalling during initial token fetch.

ryan: oncall here, grabbing it. Initial hypothesis: control-plane config fetch or auth lookup causing head-of-line stalls into the runtime.

ryan: Paging the infra + runtime folks. @sophie @samir can you join?

sophie: joining. Logs look like a lot of `config-store` 504s and `auth-service` cache misses.

samir: I see surge in requests to /config/v1/fetch for feature flags at the same time. QPS to config-store jumped x6 for a subset of customers (large batch jobs?).

maria: sample from runtime logs: ```
[2026-03-14T14:22:11Z] request_id=ixc-12345 model=redwood-1 path=/v1/stream stage=preload status=timeout msg="config fetch 504"
[2026-03-14T14:22:12Z] request_id=ixc-12346 stage=auth msg="cache-miss, fetching tokeninfo" ms=312
[2026-03-14T14:22:12Z] request_id=ixc-12346 stage=stream msg="kv-cache-miss, wait for config" ms=1021
```

sophie: that matches. Streaming stalls are often because we wait for per-request feature flags/config to decide routing/kv prefixes. If config-store is slow, the runtime stalls before token generation and streaming begins.

ryan: Can we confirm config-store is the bottleneck? samir, have you checked DB-side metrics?

samir: DB CPU for config-store instances spiked and there are a lot of short-lived connections. I see increased `pg_backend_wait` on feature_flag table locks during the window. Also our rate limiter for config-store backed off to 429s for a small percentage.

ops-bot: Synthetic check failure: GET https://config.redwood.internal/config/v1/fetch latency 850ms (baseline 35ms)

maria: So chain is: heavy config fetch QPS -> config-store/backing DB contends -> 504/429s -> runtime waits on config/auth -> streaming stalls -> p99 climbs.

sophie: Mitigation plan A (fast): 1) Fail-open on per-request feature flag resolution for streaming paths (use cached defaults). 2) Increase config cache TTL from 15s -> 5m for streaming requests. 3) Temporarily raise config-store read replicas autoscale and allow burst capacity.

ryan: Agreed. Doing A1 and A2 now. Deploying a config flag to make streaming path use cached config on miss.

samir: I'll spin up two extra read replicas and bump DB connection pool for config-store. ETA ~4m.

maria: I pushed a small runtime patch to short-circuit feature flag resolution for streaming: `if (streaming && config_cache.miss) { use_default_flags(); }` rolling to 20% canary to start.

ryan: Canary at 20% -> monitoring. p99 down to 6.1s after the change (was 12.4s). stalls reduced.

sophie: After replica add and pool bump, config-store tail latency improved. ops-bot synthetic now 78ms.

ops-bot: Synthetic check success: GET https://config.redwood.internal/config/v1/fetch latency 78ms

maria: We should also identify the source of the config surge. Querying request logs now to find customer or job causing x6 QPS.

samir: Found candidate: a customer scheduled mass inference job that started at 14:20 and does per-request feature flagging per user (no batching). Reached out to SE owner.

ryan: For now: 1) keep fail-open and raised cache TTL for streaming for 30 min. 2) Keep extra read replicas up until normal QPS for 20m. 3) Contact affected customer and ask to throttle or use batched mode. 4) Post-mortem to include: why streaming path requires per-request fetch and options for robust local caching.

maria: Customer impact: estimated 4.7% of streaming sessions experienced stalls causing increased end-to-end latency; some sessions retried and succeeded. No data loss. We should run a targeted email to affected customers and update status.redwood.com.

oncall-bot: Handoff: Ryan -> Sophie. Ryan: please provide short summary + actions for next oncall.

ryan: Handoff summary: Root cause tracked to config-store DB contention from a sudden config fetch QPS spike from a large customer job. Immediate mitigations: fail-open streaming config, increase cache TTL, scale read replicas. Impact: p99 spikes and streaming stalls ~4.7% of sessions, no data corruption. Next steps: increase config caching logic, implement rate-limits or batching guidance for customers, add circuit-breaker to runtime so that config-service failures degrade gracefully.

sophie: Acknowledged. I'll keep watch for 30m and start the post-incident follow-up doc. Assigning follow-ups: `maria` triage logs, `samir` DB tuning and autoscale safeguards, `ryan` customer comms + status page.

maria: I'll capture metrics and attach query results to the postmortem.

samir: I'll add an alert for config-store DB lock contention and make autoscaler more aggressive for read replicas.

ryan: Adding incident tags and opening postmortem. Notifying support to prepare communications. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 2026-03-14T14:34Z. Please file postmortem with timeline and follow-ups.

sophie: I'll take the ownership for the postmortem. Thanks team.
